items.title: Mayoral candidates kick off debate season in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga’s highest-profile mayoral candidates will be on the debate stage together for the first time this election season on Friday afternoon. m. They’ll present their plans for addressing key issues impacting the city’s business community, take questions from the debate moderator and engage with one another as the days and weeks count down to the Oct. 26 municipal election. Hosted by the Mississauga Board of Trade, the 2026 Mississauga Mayoral Debate on Sept. 25 will focus on important issues including economic growth, leadership, investment, infrastructure and the city’s future, organizers say. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at right, and former mayor Bonnie Crombie will debate key Mississauga business issues on Sept. 25. ” The election season’s first mayoral debate in Mississauga will also provide an opportunity “to hear directly from mayoral candidates” as they discuss issues of most importance to city businesses of all sizes. “Whether you’re a business leader, entrepreneur, professional or engaged member of the Mississauga community, this is an opportunity to hear the candidates’ perspectives and learn more about their vision for the city,” organizers said.

items.title: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants the TTC subway extended to Mississauga’s city centre. But will Doug Ford buy in?
items.summary: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants to extend Toronto’s Line 2 subway to Mississauga’s city centre. Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is proposing to extend the TTC’s Line 2 subway from Kipling to Mississauga city centre, creating a central transit hub. Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie says it’s time for an extension of the east-west Bloor-Danforth subway line to Mississauga’s city centre — and if elected she will launch a feasibility study and appeal to a subway-loving premier and a prime minister looking for nation-building projects. “Vaughan has a subway and one is being planned for both Markham and Richmond Hill. ” said Crombie in an interview. ” The Hurontario LRT or Hazel McCallion line, which is currently under construction as a north-south spine that will extend through Mississauga’s city centre into Brampton, made sense at the time of planning more than a decade ago and was the more affordable option, Crombie said. “We didn’t have the density then, but we do have the density today and we have the demand for it,” she said, adding that the idea of a subway has been very popular as she speaks to people on the campaign trail. Carolyn Parrish, who is running for re-election as mayor, has been a fan of the idea of a Mississauga subway, and lamented that McCallion shot the idea down when she was mayor decades ago. But Parrish has also cited the hefty price tag as a barrier, unless the province is willing to pick up the tab of $1 billion per kilometre. “Listen, if somebody is going to put a subway out to Mississauga, there’s no way anybody in their right mind would turn it down with traffic (as it is) now,” Parrish told Insauga last year.

items.title: Ward 1 voters in Mississauga will have two candidates on the ballot
items.summary: Mississauga Ward 1 candidates outline their backgrounds and priorities ahead of the 2026 municipal election. Two candidates are running to represent Mississauga’s Ward 1 at City Hall with one incumbent and one new candidate. OCCUPATION Ward 1 Councillor for the City of Mississauga and the Region of Peel First elected as Ward 1 city councillor and regional councillor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. I serve on numerous city and regional committees, including as chair of the Road Safety Committee, vice-chair of the Budget Committee and vice-chair of the Environmental Action Committee. DO YOU LIVE IN WARD? Yes, I am a lifelong Ward 1 resident, born and raised in the community. My priority is to continue delivering responsible, practical leadership for Ward 1 and Mississauga while ensuring residents have a strong voice at City Hall. I will continue advocating for Ward 1 to receive its fair share of investment in infrastructure, transportation, parks, public safety and community services. Public safety and road safety will remain central priorities. I will continue advocating for effective policing, community-based programs and traffic-calming measures that make our neighbourhoods safer. I will also focus on responsible growth, ensuring development follows the city’s official plan, respects existing neighbourhoods and is supported by the infrastructure and services residents need. Growth must be accompanied by appropriate infrastructure, parks, and community amenities.

items.title: Crombie proposes subway extension into Mississauga in election bid
items.summary: Mississauga mayoral hopeful Bonnie Crombie is pitching the idea of extending Toronto’s subway network into her city, hoping that, if she wins, she can convince Premier Doug Ford to fund the plan. Unveiling her transit proposals on Thursday, Crombie said she wanted to see Line 2 extended westward from Kipling Station into downtown Mississauga, with a stop at Square One via Sherway Gardens. “For the first time, residents should ultimately be able to board the subway in Mississauga and ride directly into Toronto,” Crombie wrote. “Toronto has already directed planning work on a possible Line 2 extension from Kipling to Sherway Gardens. ” Crombie served as Mississauga mayor from 2014 to 2024, leaving the post to become leader of the Ontario Liberal Party. She is running against incumbent Carolyn Parrish, as well as councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla and several other candidates to take control of city council. Tedjo’s campaign said a subway extension may be a “dream worth pursuing” but stressed a better relationship “with the province to secure the support and funding needed to make it happen” must be the first step. Damela said the key was delivering “realistic” transit.

items.title: Bonnie Crombie wants TTC Line 2 subway extended to Mississauga: ‘Should be part of that conversation’
items.summary: Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is putting transit and gridlock at the centre of her campaign, unveiling an ambitious transportation plan that includes bringing Toronto’s subway system into Mississauga. 0, the plan’s headline proposal calls for extending Toronto’s Line 2 subway west from Kipling Station through Sherway Gardens and into Mississauga, creating a direct subway connection between downtown Mississauga and Toronto for the first time. “Mississauga residents are spending too much of their lives sitting in traffic,” Crombie said while unveiling the plan Thursday. ” The subway proposal would not immediately launch construction, but Crombie says she would spend her first year in office pursuing a formal partnership with the provincial government, Metrolinx, the TTC and the City of Toronto to study the extension. The business case would examine possible routes, station locations, ridership projections, costs and construction options. Notably, Crombie said the review should explore whether portions of the route could be built above ground along the Dundas corridor rather than entirely underground, a move that could significantly reduce costs. The proposal comes as Toronto continues planning for potential future transit expansion west of Kipling and as neighbouring municipalities secure major rapid-transit investments. “Vaughan is on the subway map. Scarborough is getting a major subway extension. Mississauga should be part of that conversation too,” Crombie said.

items.title: Modular condo community gets a green light in Mississauga
items.summary: A new modular home community should be coming soon to Mississauga. The development, three six-storey condominium apartment buildings containing 141 units at 6344 Ninth Line, was approved at the City of Mississauga’s Planning and Development Committee meeting this week. The property is north of Britannia Road West, at the border with Milton. The land is currently vacant. The initial proposal was for eight-storey buildings, but area residents asked for a reduction in height, Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden said at the Sept. 21 planning meeting. Dubbed “The Nine” project in northwest Mississauga will be Mattamy’s first modular-constructed community, according to the application submitted in June. “Modular construction at The Nine will accelerate the construction timeline, allowing for quicker occupancy for buyers, and minimizing disruptions for the adjacent community,” Mattamy said in a letter to the planning committee. The condo units will be just 1,000 square feet with patios. The plans include 69 three-bedroom units, 42 two-bedroom units and 30 one-bedroom units. Plans include a central outdoor space and an underground parking area. A total of 223 parking spaces are planned, including 25 spaces at grade, with the remaining 198 in the underground parking structure. An aerial photograph shows the location of the development.

items.title: Overnight Blaze Destroys a Flatbed Tow Truck Near Pearson in Mississauga's Latest Suspicious Fire
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel police are investigating after an overnight fire destroyed a flatbed tow truck in the area of Dixie Road and Shawson Drive, in Mississauga's east end just west of Toronto Pearson Airport. Police describe the blaze, which broke out early Thursday morning, as suspicious and say it is the latest in a string of similar tow truck fires across the region. According to police, no injuries were reported as a result of the fire. Investigators say they have no information yet on a suspect or suspects. Peel police are asking anyone with information about the incident, including CCTV or dash camera footage, to contact the force's 12 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau. INsauga notes the blaze follows a similar incident on August 6, when a tow truck caught fire while parked in a driveway near Creditview Road and Sandalwood Parkway in Brampton, part of a broader pattern of tow truck fires seen across Mississauga, Brampton and the wider GTA this year and in past years.
